subject: Residual rounding on slabed bundles — quantum offset proposal
messages:

Subject: Clarify invoice rounding — leftover tokens from slabed bundles

Hi Neha,

We got the May invoice and flagged a recurring question from our billing team: when our service calls include very long contexts (mostly 40k+ token retrieval responses) some calls round up to the slab quantum and leave a residual that doesn't get consumed. Over the month those residuals add up and show as a small but steady overage.

Attached is a sample invoice line and a small extract of example calls. Can you explain: 1) how the slabed "context band" interacts with per-request token quantum rounding, and 2) whether leftover residuals can be offset in the next invoice or credited?

Our finance lead asked if Redwood has a standard approach (monthly smoothing, per-call floor, or a one-time reconciliation). Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks — Elena
Director, Platform Integrations
Alphamed

Attachment: sample-invoice-may28.pdf (invoice snippet)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify invoice rounding — leftover tokens from slabed bundles

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the invoice extract. I reviewed the sample and looped in Karthik + Markus to make sure we cover product and billing nuances. Quick summary up-front:

- Short answer: the platform currently applies quantum rounding at the invoice line level after conversation-level amortization; that means very long single calls that cross a context "band" can cause per-call rounding that leaves small residuals.
- We do not currently auto-smooth those residuals across months; smoothing is done for specific pilots or when a customer requests a consolidated reconciliation.

I'll ask the billing team to run the exact math for your sample file (please also attach the raw call IDs if available). Meanwhile, two options we can propose:

1) Operational compromise: apply a monthly residual reconciliation where we sum residuals for the account and offset them as a single invoice credit (one-off).
2) Config change: treat your workload under a "context-amortization" setting (applies at the account level) where we change the quantum to a larger aggregation window (e.g., 15-min session bucketing) so the per-call rounding happens less often. This reduces residual frequency but slightly changes unit economics.

Which would you prefer us to model? I can prepare numbers for both. Also copying Karthik/Markus for technical/contract commentary.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Clarify invoice rounding — leftover tokens from slabed bundles

Neha / team — I ran a quick sample against the workbook Neha attached. A couple technical points to call out before we give Alpha the commercial:

- Our invoice pipeline: we compute per-request tokenization -> apply the "quantum" rounding rule (configurable per account; default 8 tokens) -> group calls into the customer's selected context band for amortization if configured -> finalize invoice lines. The residuals Elena references are the leftover after the quantum step but before amortization, which means they can persist if calls are sparse.

- Example: a single 40,512-token call on a 4k slab triggers slab billing for 40k+ banding and then the quantum rounds the per-token charge in the last partial quantum. The residual (e.g., 6 tokens) is not currently carried forward unless you select monthly residual reconciliation.

Commercial options we can offer:
A) One-time credit equal to the sum of measured residuals for May (we should offer a cap, e.g., up to 3% of the invoice)
B) Apply an account-level change to the quantum (increase to 32 tokens) and enable 15-minute amortization windows for long-context calls (reduces residuals materially; shows as a ~1.8% invoice uplift in our model for similar traffic)
C) Pilot a smoothing policy (monthly) where residuals are summed and netted each invoice automatically for a trial period (3 months) — this will be a bookkeeping change only.

I'd recommend starting with A + B: immediate one-time credit for May while enabling the config change for June forward. If Finance asks for net-neutrality in the first month, we can reduce the credit cap. Markus / Marissa: any legal/accounting flags?

-Karthik

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Alphamed Billing <billing@alphamed.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify invoice rounding — leftover tokens from slabed bundles

Elena — thanks for the patience. We modeled the two approaches and propose the following practical path: 

1) Immediate one-time credit: Redwood will issue a one-time invoice credit for May equal to the measured residuals in your sample, capped at 2.5% of the May invoice. (We measured $4,120 in residuals on the sample; full-month run shows ~$5,150 — we'll cap at $4,500 for this one-off.)

2) Configuration change (effective June 1): switch Alphamed to 32-token quantum and enable a 15-minute amortization window for calls flagged as "long-context retrieval". Our simulation projects residuals to drop by ~88% with a negligible 1.6% increase in billable units due to larger quantum aggregation.

3) Trial smoothing: if you'd like, we can run the monthly smoothing pilot (3 months) to validate the numbers; after 3 months we'll reconvene and either bake the smoothing into standard invoicing or revert.

Action items:
- Elena: reply to confirm you accept the one-time credit + config change for June, or tell us if you want the smoothing pilot instead.
- Alphamed Billing: please send raw call IDs (or a short export of May call timestamps + call sizes) so we're working off the same dataset.

If you prefer a short call to finalize, I'm free Friday 9–11am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
